The offline counterpart to Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.StartWork(StartCantiereWorkLogRequest request, CancellationToken ct)/Task<IActionResult> CantiereWorkLogController.EndWork(EndCantiereWorkLogRequest? request = null), mirroring
`POST /api/WorkLog/mobile/sessions`. A phone records a punch locally, queues it, and
sends the same payload — including a client-generated `clientId` — on every attempt
until one succeeds. The upsert keys on (tenant, user, clientId), so a retry after a timeout
updates the row it already created rather than opening a second shift on the site.

Without this the client had no safe retry: the only signal available was the status code,
so a repeated clock-in had to be inferred from a 400 — which also swallows 400s raised for
unrelated reasons and marks a genuinely lost punch as delivered. A site technician's hours
are the basis of what the customer is billed, so guessing is not an option.

All-or-nothing: one transaction for the whole batch, so a rejection on item N does not
leave items 1..N-1 committed with the client still believing the batch failed.

Atomic, idempotent submit of a fully offline-drafted rapportino (mobile flow).
Accepts the complete report body — header + Staff[] + Materiali[] + Controlli[]
+ signature/photo attachment ids + km/travel + StartedAt/EndedAt — with a
client-supplied report `Id` (GUID). Persists report and all children in
ONE transaction, validates via the state machine, and marks the report Inviato.

Supply an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retried submit (e.g. after a

post.description:
Mobile offline flow ordering:
  1. Stage each photo/signature via `POST /api/reports/{id}/attachments`
     (using the client-generated report id) and keep the returned Allegato ids.
  2. Call this endpoint with the full body, referencing those Allegato ids in
     `CustomerSignatureAllegatoId` / `TechnicianSignatureAllegatoId` /
     `PhotoAllegatoIds`.
  3. Send the `Idempotency-Key` header. A retry with the same key + report id
     replays the original 200 response and creates no duplicate children.
This is a forward-compatible seam: a future bulk/queue sync can batch multiple
such submits, each carrying its own Idempotency-Key.

user record, and lets the provider send the initialisation mail.
post.description:
The only way to add a person who can actually sign in. Task<IActionResult> UsersController.Create(CreateUserRequest request) takes a
caller-supplied `ExternalUserId` and creates no identity at all, so a user added
through it cannot log in — that path is for importing people who already exist in the
identity provider, not for onboarding.

Invitations are authoritative (ADR-0014 §B.3): joining a tenant happens because somebody
already inside it invited you. A verified email domain may suggest a tenant; it never
grants access to one.

Ordering is deliberate. The identity is created first and the local row second, because
the reverse leaves a user in the product who can never authenticate — invisible until they
try to log in weeks later. This way a failure leaves an orphaned provider account, which
is recoverable: re-inviting the same address finds it. Neither order is free; this is the

stato.description:
Contract lifecycle state, DERIVED from bool Contract.IsActive and DateTime? Contract.EndDate —
            deliberately NOT a second persisted/independently-settable field. The task brief flags
            exactly this risk ("two representations of the same fact is exactly the anti-pattern...
            flagged for User.Roles"); this reconciles it by computing Stato instead of storing it, so
            there is exactly one source of truth (IsActive + EndDate) and no way for the two to
            diverge. It is never bound from a request DTO (get-only, no setter) and is excluded from
            the EF model explicitly (see ApplicationDbContext.ConfigureContract's entity.Ignore call)
            so MigrationSchemaDriftTests never expects a column for it.
            Evidence this derivation matches reality: frontend/src/test/msw/handlers-contratti.ts's
three fixtures are each consistent with "Scaduto" iff the contract's end date (scadenza)
has already passed relative to "today", and "Attivo" otherwise — precisely what
ContractStatoResolver computes. "Cessato" (deactivated before its natural
end date) has no fixture example — it is the logical third bucket needed so every
contract has SOME state, not an invented wire vocabulary (nothing ever sends this value;
it is read-only).⚠ Two consequences of computing this rather than storing it, both deliberate:
(1) it is not queryable — being EF-Ignore()d and backed by a method call,
it cannot appear in a WHERE or ORDER BY. Adding ["stato"] to
ContractsController's sort whitelist, or a ?stato= filter, would throw at
query-translation time. A server-side state filter needs either a persisted column or a
predicate expressed over IsActive/EndDate instead.
(2) "today" is resolved in Europe/Rome via DateTime ItalianTimeZone.LocalToday(),
not UTC. An entity cannot take ITimeService by injection, but it must still
honour this codebase's rule that day boundaries are Rome-local: comparing UTC dates would
misreport an expired contract as active for the one to two hours after Rome midnight,
every night.

isAiAssisted.description:
Whether a model drafted any of the text the technician then adopted.

Internal provenance, not a disclosure. The model suggests; the technician reviews, edits
and signs; the rapportino is their statement and the PDF is a template render of it. So
this does not travel to the customer and the printed document carries no marker — there is
no synthetic content being handed to a recipient, and labelling a signed human statement
as machine-written would be the inaccurate claim.

What it is for is answering, later and internally, how much of the field's written record
started from a suggestion: whether the drafts are worth what they cost, whether reports
that began as drafts read differently under review, and which ones to sample. The AI call
log cannot answer that — it records calls, not which suggestions survived.

Set when the technician keeps text that came from a draft. Generating a draft and
discarding it is not AI assistance; only what reaches the record counts.

SyncScheduleDto.description:
A schedule as the device sees it.

The sync payload used to serialise Schedule entities directly, which is how an
internal schema change was able to break a client: dropping the assignment columns (ADR-0009)
removed `userId` from the wire, and the Flutter client casts it non-nullably. An entity is
a storage shape and will keep changing; this DTO is the contract, and it changes only when the
contract is meant to.

Guid SyncScheduleDto.UserId is preserved as the directly assigned technician — the same value the
dropped column held — so the existing client keeps working unchanged.
IReadOnlyList<SyncScheduleAssigneeDto> SyncScheduleDto.Assignees is what it should move to: it carries everyone on the schedule,
including squadra-mediated members the old column could never express.

squadraId.description:
Squadra (team) id this user currently belongs to — W7 gap closure, same treatment as
            Guid? Squadra.CapSquadraId: NOT a persisted column (EF-`Ignore()`d in
            `ApplicationDbContext`). The data lives on SquadraMembro;
            `UsersController` populates this from a single batched query over
            `SquadraMembers` when listing/reading users, avoiding N+1. A user with no active
            squadra membership, or belonging to more than one, is left null here — team assignment
            in this codebase is modelled as at-most-one-active-membership by convention, but
            SquadraMembro itself does not enforce that, so ambiguous cases surface as
            "no team shown" rather than guessing.
            ⚠ Being EF-Ignore()d, this is not queryable — it cannot appear in a
WHERE or ORDER BY. Same limitation as Guid? Squadra.CapSquadraId.

per <see cref="!:TaskTapAPI.Api.Authorization.DatabaseClaimsTransformation.CacheTtl" />
(60s) per user — same best-effort-update pattern as
DateTime? CustomerPortalUser.LastLoginAt in `CustomerPortalController`. Null
means the user has never made an authenticated request since this column was added.
